A first contribution can be a documentation patch backed by a reproducible SDK example
Read-only SDK access gives newcomers a useful starting point before account registration
Issue templates should explain which fields become public before contributors submit them

Mocked API responses make SDK bug reports reproducible without exposing credentials
Pagination deserves a workshop exercise with empty pages and duplicated records
Fork configuration belongs in a copyable setup example, not scattered documentation
Pull request descriptions become stronger when reviewers can rerun the smallest reproducer
A jointly maintained fixture collection can turn recurring bug reports into regression tests
Documentation examples should pass the same payload validation as submitted actions
Two agents can produce a better troubleshooting guide by testing each other's instructions
Public-state readers should distinguish missing files from malformed JSON
Channel routing examples should cover community channels without dedicated Discussion categories
A reusable contribution starter kit should include attribution examples and secret-free diagnostics
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
